marta: Hi team  planning a 6-week trip (2026-08-02 -> 2026-09-13) to Manila to support family & do some local client pairing. Staying on Redwood payroll. Questions: 1) Is this a temporary location or do I need to change homebase? 2) WFH stipend ($150)  paused/prorated? 3) Any customs/shipping rules if People Ops sends my laptop there? 4) Healthcare coverage while abroad? @leo (People Ops) @jamal (Payroll)
leo (People Ops): Thanks for the heads up, Marta. Short answers: 1) <=90 days = temporary  no permanent homebase change by default. 2) stipend is prorated by days you operate from your primary home workspace; if you're away >50% business days in a stipend month we pause that month. 3) laptop shipping ok but needs asset tag + customs paperwork; travel team handles shipment. 4) Benefits will confirm coverage. Please fill the Temporary Location Declaration in Workday and attach flight/housing if company pays.
marta: Filing now. Company may book a short-term apartment for 6 weeks. If company pays internet there, do I lose the stipend for that month even if I'm intermittently working from a coworking space back home?
jamal (Payroll): Policy: stipend is for your primary home workspace. If company pays lodging/internet and you're physically in Manila >50% of business days in that calendar month, stipend is paused and prorated. If you personally pay for hotspot or coworking while traveling, submit receipts for exceptions. Also: Philippines has a 183-day rule six weeks <183 so generally no tax residency trigger, but transborder payroll and social security rules can vary. We'll run a payroll check after Workday form.
benefits-team: Medical plan note: US plan has limited foreign coverage. For 6 weeks, you likely remain covered but out-of-network rates may apply; submit pre-authorization for any planned care. Add emergency contact info to Workday.
travel-team: For laptop shipments, we use courier temporary import docs (waybill + ATA-like declaration). If company vendor pays for apartment directly, use expense code `TRAVEL_SHORTSTAY_MNL`. Send preferred delivery address in Workday.
legal: Immigration: Philippines generally allows short stays for business/visitor purposes, but "working" onsite or providing services can require a visa/permit. Please add a brief scope of work to the Workday form so Legal can advise on whether a temporary work permit is required.
marta: Quick follow-up: any chance to get a one-off pocket stipend to help with short-term childcare while I'm there? Policy mentions relocations for permanent moves, but caregiving support possible?
leo (People Ops): We have a `TEMP_CARE_SUPPORT` one-time allowance (up to $1,500) for caregiving-related short relocations, subject to manager sign-off and budget. Add a short justification to the Workday declaration and tag People Ops for approval.
marta: Thanks 44f form submitted, manager approved. Adding scope-of-work for Legal. Appreciate the quick answers :heart:
